newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank of Italy declines comment on gold reserves.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Italy declines comment on gold reserves.

text.p: The Bank of Italy declined any comment on whether or not there were plans to revalue Italian gold reserves in the wake of a proposal by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel to revalue Bundesbank gold reserves.

According to latest data from March, Italian gold reserves were worth 37.49 trillion lire against 39.54 trillion lire the same month last year. The exact weight of the reserves was not immediately available.

Waigel said this week he wanted Bundesbank gold and currency reserves to be revalued from current low book prices to levels close to the normal market price, in a bid to plug a hole in state accounts.

Italy has introduced around 100 trillion lire of deficit cutting measures over the last year as it fights to make the grade for the single European currency, but there has never been any suggestion that the government would revalue or sell gold assets to improve accounts. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
